app.title: Browser tab title (HTML <title>) of web pages that don't set their own. The product name, Fivvi, the same in both languages.
app.name: Name of the native app under its home-screen icon (iOS CFBundleDisplayName and CFBundleName, Android app label). The name of the trainer app, Fivvi Pro, the same in both languages.
common.loading: Accessibility label of the progress indicator while a screen loads (read by VoiceOver and TalkBack).
common.retry: Button under an error message that tries the failed action again.
hello.description: Line under the title of the hello page, above the first-name field.
hello.firstNameLabel: Label of the first-name field on the hello page.
hello.continue: Submit button of the first-name form on the hello page. Shows hello.formGreeting with the name entered.
hello.formGreeting: Shown on the hello page after the first-name form is sent. {name} is the first name entered.
hello.greeting: Greeting above the home screen. {name} is the user's first name.
hello.sessionsToday: Number of sessions the trainer has today, 1 or more. For 0, use hello.noSessionsToday.
hello.nextSession: {date} is a weekday and date without year, e.g. 'dinsdag 22 september'. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '18:00'. Both are formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
hello.error: Shown on the native hello screen when the greeting can't be loaded (no connection, or an unknown greeting). Above the common.retry button.
home.setUpOnWeb: Native home when the account has no workspace but may set one up. Creating a workspace happens on the web only; this line tells the person to do that. Above home.openWeb.
home.openWeb: Button under home.setUpOnWeb in the native apps; opens Fivvi on the web (the first-run screen) in the phone's browser.
email.layout.footer: Last line of every email, below the content.
email.hello.subject: Subject of the test email that checks email delivery (E006). Only sent by the team, never to clients.
email.hello.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject.
email.hello.greeting: {firstName} is the recipient's first name. When unknown, use email.hello.greetingWithoutName.
email.hello.sentAt: {date} is a weekday and date with year, e.g. 'dinsdag 29 september 2026'. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '18:00'. Both are formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
email.signIn.subject: Subject of EM-08, the sign-in email. Contains the code and a sign-in link (inloglink).
email.signIn.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {code} is the 6-digit sign-in code.
email.signIn.intro: Line above the 6-digit sign-in code, which is shown on its own line below it.
email.signIn.linkIntro: Line above the sign-in link. The link opens a confirmation page; nothing is signed in until the person presses its button.
email.signIn.linkButton: Label of the button that opens the sign-in link (the confirmation page).
email.signIn.validity: {minutes} is how many minutes the code and the sign-in link work, e.g. 15.
email.signIn.ignore: Last line of the sign-in email, for someone who did not ask for it.
signIn.title: Heading of the first step of the sign-in page (TW-10), where the email address is entered, and the browser tab title of the page.
signIn.emailLabel: Label of the email field on the sign-in page.
signIn.sendCode: Button under the email field of the sign-in page. Sends one email with a 6-digit code and a sign-in link.
signIn.checkEmailTitle: Heading of the second step of the sign-in page, shown after the email address was sent. Same wording whether or not the address has an account.
signIn.checkEmailBody: Under the heading of the second step. {email} is the address that was entered. Deliberately does not say whether an account exists (no account enumeration).
signIn.checkEmailBodyApp: Native apps only (TM-01): under the heading of the code step, instead of signIn.checkEmailBody. {email} is the address entered. Says the email has a code, without the sign-in link: a link tapped on the phone signs in the phone's browser, not the app. The instruction to enter the code comes from signIn.codeHelp. Deliberately does not say whether an account exists (no account enumeration).
signIn.codeLabel: Label of the field for the 6-digit code from the email (one-time-code autofill on phones). The word alone; the sentence is signIn.codeHelp.
signIn.codeHelp: Helper text under the code field on the second step of the sign-in page. The field is described by it.
signIn.submitCode: Button that signs in with the code that was entered.
signIn.resend: Button on the second step that sends a new email. The new code replaces the old one.
signIn.resent: Confirmation after a new email was requested. {email} is the address entered. Does not say whether an account exists.
signIn.changeEmail: Button on the second step that goes back to the email field.
signIn.confirmChecking: Shown for a moment on the confirm step (TW-10) while the page checks the sign-in link from the email. Checking uses nothing up.
signIn.confirmTitle: Heading of the confirm step, where the sign-in link from the email lands. {email} is the masked address the link signs in, e.g. j***@example.com.
signIn.confirmSubmit: The one button of the confirm step. Pressing it uses up the link and signs this browser in.
signIn.linkInvalidTitle: Heading of the confirm step when the link no longer works. One message for an expired, used or replaced link: it never says which.
signIn.linkInvalidBody: Line under signIn.linkInvalidTitle, pointing to the button that goes back to the sign-in page.
signIn.linkInvalidBack: Button on the confirm step for a link that no longer works. Goes back to the sign-in page, where a new email is requested.
signIn.signedOutNotice: Native apps only: notice at the top of the sign-in screen (TM-01) when the app was signed out without the person asking: the server no longer accepts the stored sign-in, or the person signed out elsewhere. Not shown after the person signs out in the app.
signIn.errors.invalidEmail: Under the email field when the address is empty or not an email address.
signIn.errors.invalidOrExpiredCode: Shown when the code was refused. One message for a wrong, expired, used or replaced code: it never says which.
signIn.errors.noConnection: Shown when the sign-in request could not reach the server.
signIn.errors.generic: Shown when sign-in failed for any other reason.
home.signedInAs: Native apps only: line on the signed-in home placeholder that says which account is signed in. {email} is the account's email address, shown in full to its owner.
welcome.title: Heading of TW-11, the first-run screen (`/welcome`) shown once to an operator-approved person who has no workspace yet. Fivvi is the product name.
welcome.description: Line under the heading of TW-11.
welcome.personNameLabel: Label of the field for the person's own name on TW-11. Shown only when the account has no name yet.
welcome.workspaceNameLabel: Label of the field for the name of the gym or business on TW-11. The workspace itself, worded as the person's own business (GLOSSARY §4.1: prefer this over the word werkruimte).
welcome.workspaceNameHint: Hint under the workspace name field on TW-11: an example of a name. "John's Gym" is a name, the same in both languages.
welcome.submit: Submit button of TW-11. It creates the workspace and opens it.
welcome.errors.personNameRequired: Under the name field on TW-11 when it is empty or only spaces.
welcome.errors.personNameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-11 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
welcome.errors.workspaceNameRequired: Under the workspace name field on TW-11 when it is empty or only spaces.
welcome.errors.workspaceNameTooLong: Under the workspace name field on TW-11 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
welcome.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-11 when the request to create the workspace could not reach the server. Nothing was created.
welcome.errors.generic: Shown on TW-11 when creating the workspace failed for any other reason. Nothing was created.
noAccess.title: Heading of the no-access page: a signed-in person who is not in a workspace and may not create one (a client, or someone who was removed). The page has the sign-out button.
noAccess.body: Text of the no-access page (information-architecture §9.5, No permission). Native apps show it too, under the same conditions. The Dutch uses 'werkruimte' as the spec words it.
workspaceHome.description: Line under the workspace name on the placeholder home of a workspace, until the owner dashboard and the trainer's day arrive.
signOut.label: Button that signs out only the browser (or device) it is pressed on; other browsers stay signed in. On every signed-in page of the web app.
signOut.error: Shown next to the sign-out button when signing out failed (no connection or a server error). The person is still signed in and can try again.
